agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager sees an honest but generic teacher letter that admits the GMP gap without proof of regulated-style documentation, so a phone screen is possible but not likely.

honest.reason: It wisely drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' claim, but adds unsupported details: 'working safely and independently within days', 'nine years of reading regulations' and 'learning new classroom systems', when the brief mentions only Google Classroom.

works_the_facts.reason: It gets seven injury-free years from 2019 but leaves out the strongest figures: the 20-to-12-hour cut (40%), about 18 teachers trained, and two clean state audits of signed training records.

right_comparison.reason: The only fair 'before' benchmark, the old 20-hour new-teacher training, is missing, so the promise to cut the plant's training time has nothing to compare against.

qualification.reason: The gap is hedged with a vague 'I expect to learn quickly' instead of checkable terms such as the GMP course finishing May 2, the June 14 start date or interview availability.

objections.reason: It names the GMP-records objection but doesn't answer it with the facts that would: signed training records for every trainee, two clean state audits and the GMP course already underway.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right form, but it uses placeholders even though Laura Benitez, Calder Pharmaceuticals, Westfield and Karen Doyle were all known.
